title: How the Manpower Ministry defines and tracks 'good jobs'
asked: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat asked for the Ministry's operational definition of a "good job" as used in the Economic Strategy Review, the measurable indicators it will use to track whether the strategy creates such jobs, and whether it will adopt a multi-dimensional job quality framework comparable to the OECD's.
response: Dr Koh Poh Koon said the Ministry uses wages as its key operational measure of whether proposed investments create good jobs, while noting that a good job varies between individuals and that there is no single accepted framework for measuring job quality. It tracks labour market participation, labour underutilisation and earnings, which he said are broadly aligned with the OECD framework. He cited real median gross monthly income growth of 7.4% from 2021 to 2025, 10.1% growth at the 20th percentile, structured training at two-thirds of private sector establishments, and a fall in reported workplace discrimination from 8.5% in 2021 to 6% in 2023. On the supplementary questions, he said wage share could be included among the dimensions measured, and that trades and skilled roles are still under deliberation by the Economic Strategy Review.

key_points.point: Wages are the Ministry's key operational measure for whether investments create good jobs.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: we use wages as a key operational measure to track if proposed investments create good jobs

key_points.point: There is no single, universally accepted framework for measuring job quality.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: no single, universally accepted framework for measuring job quality

key_points.point: The Ministry tracks three labour market indicators: participation, underutilisation and earnings.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: one, labour market participation; two, labour underutilisation; and three, earnings

key_points.point: These indicators are broadly aligned with the OECD framework.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: These are broadly aligned with the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) framework

key_points.point: Real gross monthly income at the median grew 7.4% from 2021 to 2025.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: From 2021 to 2025, real gross monthly income at the median grew by 7.4%.

key_points.point: Income at the 20th percentile grew 10.1% over the same period.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: At the 20th percentile, income grew even faster, by 10.1% over the same period.

key_points.point: Two-thirds of private sector establishments provided structured training to employees.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: Two-thirds of private sector establishments provided structured training to employees

key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
